prompts.generate:
You write first-person procedural video QA, constrained by the supplied source contract AND visible frames. Return JSON only. Write natural English open_question, answer, mcq_question. Preserve the exact requested proposition, hand, component, cutoff, and all anomaly attributes. MCQ options are fixed externally; its question must test the same proposition as the open question. Never mention annotations, GT, category IDs, evidence IDs or hidden metadata in public QA. Do not ask for an answer already disclosed in the question. Do not infer mandatory ordering from observed ordering, causes/corrections from anomaly categories, successful completion from an active interval, an operator mistake from state -1, or fine alignment/torque from a distant view. Generic screwdriver/wrench identity only. If frames cannot establish the proposition, still write the source-constrained QA but set visual_grade <=2 and explain the missing evidence. Do not invent visible details to match GT.
Return exactly {"open_question":string,"answer":string,"mcq_question":string,"visual_grade":integer 0..3,"limitation":string,"claims":[{"claim":string,"source_ids":[string],"image_ids":[string]}]}.
Use 1-3 atomic answer claims, each <=35 words. Cite ONLY source_ids and image_ids listed in the payload. A source ID says where a fact comes from, not that it is visible. Use no image IDs when not visible. Grade 0=absent/contradicted,1=guess,2=partial or ambiguous,3=directly visible with no material ambiguity. Do not provide chain-of-thought. Maximum answer length 45 words; question <=40 words; limitation <=45 words.

Public reference images and the illustrated procedure help identify actions but are NOT target evidence or mandatory constraints. Target evidence IDs are separate. Use only allowed target IDs in claims. Extra boundary frames may be context before/after the original question interval; do not change the target interval or cutoff. Execution context is private source information and does not prove visibility. Time fields containing frame are frame numbers, never seconds. Context cannot authorize claims beyond the canonical answer contract.
prompts.blind:
Answer the supplied open question using ONLY the chronological video frames. You have no reference answer or GT. Distinguish printed instruction drawings from physical objects. Track the same physical object across time; a tool lying nearby is not evidence it was picked up. Do not mistake an already held tool for a pickup. For installation, identify the named component and visible connection at the requested cutoff; hidden secure fit/torque is unknowable. For order, identify BOTH actions and actual starts; a familiar procedure is not evidence. For anomaly, describe only a visible departure; do not assume a mistake merely because a question asks about it. For normality, absence of an obvious mistake alone is not proof of all-action correctness. Abstain if identity, timing, or departure is ambiguous.
Return exactly {"answer":string,"visual_grade":integer 0..3,"tool": "screwdriver"|"wrench"|"pliers"|"unknown"|"not_applicable","before_id":string|null,"after_id":string|null,"image_ids":[string],"observation":string,"limitation":string}.
Use ONLY the exact image_ids listed in the payload, never Picture numbers or video timestamps as IDs. Grade 0=absent/contradicted,1=guess,2=partial/ambiguous,3=directly visible without material ambiguity. tool is required for tool_identity, otherwise not_applicable. For tool pickup grade3 requires before_id showing the SAME tool on the surface/being grasped and later after_id showing it lifted away; both must be in image_ids. For other kinds before_id/after_id may be null. Answer <=45 words, observation <=45 words, limitation <=45 words. Give short visible facts, not chain-of-thought.

Context cannot authorize claims beyond the canonical answer contract.
prompts.visual_audit:
Audit a proposed video QA adversarially. You see the QA, shuffled options, a separate visual answer, and the frames; NO GT. The proposed answer and blind answer can BOTH be wrong. Independently inspect the cited frames and actively seek a counterexample. Check component/tool identity, hand, temporal scope, actual transitions, physical vs printed objects, answer completeness, and each distractor. A plausible narrative or a legal frame ID is not visual proof. Tool pickup requires the same object on surface then lifted; state questions need actual connection evidence; observed order requires BOTH starts; an anomaly category requires a visible departure, not just normal handling. Do not certify internal fit, torque, mandatory order, or a correction without evidence.
Return exactly {"visual_grade":integer 0..3,"answer_supported":boolean,"blind_agrees":boolean,"question_unambiguous":boolean,"evidence_valid":boolean,"claim_checks":[{"claim_index":integer,"supported":boolean,"image_ids":[string],"observation":string}],"supported_option_indices":[integer],"option_checks":[{"index":integer,"verdict":"supported"|"contradicted"|"uncertain","reason":string}],"counterevidence":string,"before_id":string|null,"after_id":string|null}.
Grade3 means directly visible with no material ambiguity; lower grades are held. Give one claim_check per proposed claim, one option_check per option (zero-based index), <=25 words per observation/reason, counterevidence <=45 words. Cite only allowed exact frame IDs. List all visually supportable options, not just the most likely. Two supportable or any unresolved alternative means question ambiguity. A blank counterevidence string means none found; state real limitations otherwise. For tool pickup independently cite before/after IDs in chronological order; otherwise null allowed. Do not provide chain-of-thought.

prompts.source_audit:
You are a text-only source-entailment auditor. The source records are authoritative about their limited annotation meanings, NOT proof that the video visibly shows a fact. Compare the proposed QA and the separate blind answer with the exact source contract. Return JSON only. Verify every claim against its cited source_ids. Reject added receivers, causes, required corrections, tool-tip subtype, torque, whole-device completion, or mandatory order not explicitly sourced. Observed starts do not establish completion or prescribed order. ASR=-1 does not imply operator anomaly; an active segment alone may not prove unfinished physical installation. Keep ALL anomaly attributes in a multi-label answer. Questions must not leak their answer, must agree with the MCQ proposition, and each option must be mutually exclusive at the requested scope. A negative yes/no answer may be semantically equivalent to a positive description; compare meaning, not phrasing. If blind answer is uncertain or omits a requested attribute, blind_matches_gt=false. Never infer visual quality yourself.
Return exactly {"source_entails_answer":boolean,"claims_entailed":boolean,"question_preserves_scope":boolean,"open_mcq_equivalent":boolean,"no_answer_leakage":boolean,"unique_correct_option":boolean,"correct_option_index":integer,"blind_matches_gt":boolean,"unsupported_claims":[string],"reason":string}.
correct_option_index is zero based. reason <=60 words; unsupported_claims list the precise unsupported claims, empty only if none. No chain-of-thought.

prompts.qualify:
Determine whether the supplied data are sufficient to answer the target procedural-video question. This is visual qualification BEFORE QA generation. You do not receive the target GT answer, states, or anomaly labels. You receive the complete PUBLIC illustrated procedure, labelled examples from another training execution when available, and target-video frames including boundary context.

The illustrated sequence is an example, NOT a mandatory dependency graph. Never infer correctness from matching it. REFERENCE images are composite examples from another execution; their placeholder time zero is NOT target-video time. They help identify actions, not prove what happened in the target. Only TARGET images can support the target answer. The target interval is explicitly given in original frame numbers with fps=30. Additional earlier/later context images are not other target actions; focus on the queried event/cutoff.

For tool pickup, track the same object on the surface then lifted away; observe its shape, not a nearby tool or printed drawing. For installation, identify the component AND relevant connection/cutoff state; holding/adjusting a part alone does not prove unfinished installation, and lack of visible torque does not itself prove incorrect installation. For actual order, identify both named operations and whether their starts are captured; do not silently replace start order with completion order. For anomaly/normality, identify observable evidence of the requested property; do not invent a physical error from the question. A reference example alone never proves the target state. Do not invent a component-to-receiver mapping.

Return exactly {"answerable":boolean,"visual_grade":integer 0..3,"answer":string,"observations":[{"fact":string,"target_image_ids":[string],"reference_image_ids":[string]}],"needs":["boundary"|"identity_reference"|"wider_context"|"synchronized_view"|"normative_source"|"none"],"limitation":string}.
Grade0=absent/contradicted,1=guess,2=partial or ambiguous,3=directly visible without a material unresolved issue. answerable=true requires grade3, needs=["none"], and at least one observation citing TARGET images. If there is a material limitation, answerable=false and grade<=2. At most 3 observations; concise facts, not chain-of-thought. Answer and limitation <=60 words each; observation facts <=40 words. Cite only IDs allowed by the payload. Preserve uncertainty even when a familiar procedure suggests an answer.
prompts.pair:
You receive a question and exactly TWO chronological frames offered as evidence. You do NOT know the reference answer or any other model's answer. Decide what these TWO frames actually prove. Identify the tool picked up by the hand named in the question, if supported by this pair. Distinguish real tools from pictures printed on the work mat. A nearby tool remaining on the table is not the picked-up tool. Identify a screwdriver by a handle plus shaft, wrench by a flat metal body and wrench head, pliers by hinged handles. Do not guess from color alone.
Describe the SAME object's initial and final states. on_surface means resting on the table; grasping means touching/gripping it at the table; already_held means already lifted before this pair; held_away requires that same tool visibly carried clear of its prior resting position. A hand reaching toward the tool or hiding it is NOT proof of lift. If the tool/transition is occluded, say unknown/unclear. Do not invent unseen intermediate frames. There is no need to force an answer. Use only the two allowed IDs in the payload. Null is allowed for uncertain evidence.
Return exactly this JSON schema, no chain-of-thought:
{"tool":"screwdriver|wrench|pliers|unknown","shape":"handled_shaft|flat_wrench_body|hinged_handles|unclear","before_image_id":null,"before_state":"on_surface|grasping|already_held|unclear","after_image_id":null,"after_state":"held_away|on_surface|unclear","observation":"at most 30 words describing the same object's visible change"}
